name: Question 1
problem: Find a tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=(1-t)\,i-{t}^{2}\,j+(2t+1)\,k$ at the point $P(2,-1,-1).$
worked_solution:
The point $P(2,-1,-1)$ is at the tip of $r(t)$ for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t.$ At this point, the vector ${r}^{′}({t}_{0})$ is tangent to the curve.

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to $P.$ We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =2\,i-j-k \\ (1-t)\,i-{t}^{2}\,j+(2t+1)\,k & =2\,i-j-k,\end{aligned}
$$

and equating the coefficients of $i,j,$ and $k$ yields the following system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}1-t=2 \\ -{t}^{2}=-1 \\ 2t+1=-1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we get $t=-1.$ This value also satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, $P(2,-1,-1)$ is at the tip of the vector $r(-1).$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{t}^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t+1)\,k \\  & =-i-2t\,j+2\,k \\ {r}^{′}(-1) & =-i-2(-1)\,j+2\,k \\  & =-i+2\,j+2\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a tangent vector to the given curve at the point $P(2,-1,-1)$ is $-i+2\,j+2\,k.$
